---
title: "Report and article"
subtitle: "Two report layouts, a book project, and a single column article."
description: "The report type in its compact and full layouts, Quarto books, the article type with margin notes and a CRediT table, and how the extension shows authors."
---

## Compact report

The compact report is the default type.
It has no cover.
The title block, the abstract box and the body start on page 1.

```yaml
title: "Quarterly review"
author: "Mickaël Canouil"
abstract: "A short summary of the review."
format: mcanouil-typst
```

This front matter gives the same result:

```yaml
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    type: report
    layout: compact
```

## Full report

The full layout adds a cover, a main contents, one divider per chapter, a chapter contents page, and a closing page.

```yaml
title: "Clinical study report"
version: "Version 1.2"
license: "CC BY 4.0"
format: mcanouil-typst
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    type: report
    layout: full
    chapter-toc-depth: 2
```

- In a single document, each level 1 heading is a chapter.
- Each chapter divider shows the chapter number, the title and one line of introduction.
- The introduction line is the `description` attribute of the heading, or else the first sentence of the first paragraph.
- The chapter contents page ("In this chapter") lists the sections to the depth of `chapter-toc-depth`. Each entry is a link.
- The closing page shows the contact of each author with an email or an ORCID, the licence and copyright, and a colophon.

```markdown
# Methods {description="How the study was designed and run."}
```

In `mcanouil-html`, the full layout renders as the compact one.
Each chapter gets a chapter header with its number, its title and the "In this chapter" list.

## Book project

`mcanouil-typst` renders a Quarto book as a full report.
Each book chapter is a chapter, and `book: appendices:` gives the lettered appendices.

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "Clinical study report"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - sections/01-design.qmd
    - sections/02-references.qmd
  appendices:
    - sections/appendix-a-listings.qmd

format:
  mcanouil-typst: default
  mcanouil-html:
    toc: true

extensions:
  mcanouil:
    type: report
    layout: full
```

A `description` in the front matter of a chapter file gives its introduction line.
In `mcanouil-html`, the book keeps the navigation and search of Quarto, with the style of the preset.

## Article

```yaml
title: "A short paper"
abstract: "What the paper shows."
keywords: [quarto, typst]
bibliography: references.bib
format: mcanouil-typst
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    type: article
```

The article has one column and a wide outer margin for margin notes and asides.
It has a tinted abstract box, keywords, numbered headings and numbered references.
The `.column-margin` div and the `reference-location: margin` option put content in the margin.

## Authors {#authors}

The extension reads the authors that Quarto normalises, with no keys of its own.

```yaml
author:
  - name: Ana Author
    degrees: PhD
    orcid: 0000-0002-0724-1961
    email: ana@example.org
    corresponding: true
    equal-contributor: true
    affiliations:
      - name: Example University
        city: Lille
    roles:
      - role: conceptualization
        degree-of-contribution: lead
      - role: software
        degree-of-contribution: supporting
```

- Degrees show in small type after the name.
- Affiliations get numbers.
- A corresponding author gets an envelope mark, and an equal contributor an asterisk, each with a legend line.
- An ORCID shows as a badge with a text alternative.

In an article, the CRediT roles give a table at the end: one row per role, one column per author.
The marks are L (lead), E (equal) and S (supporting), with a legend.

## Block quotes

If the last paragraph of a block quote starts with `--`, an en dash or an em dash, it is the attribution.
The dash does not show, and the attribution has the style of the preset.

```markdown
> Design for the reader who cannot see the colours.
>
> -- Mickaël Canouil, 2026
```
